## Overview

This report provides a dynamic, interactive dashboard that aggregates 10 years of historical stock data from NASDAQ. It quantifies the speed, frequency, and magnitude of price changes (volatility) for ten major watchlisted companies, offering professional, sector-focused financial insights.

---

## Price Volatility & Rapidity Analysis

"Rapidity of price change" measures how fast and widely stock values fluctuate. Below is the historical ranking of the watchlisted companies, sorted from **most volatile** (fastest changing) to **most stable** (slowest changing).

::: {.custom-card}
### Rapidity & Volatility Ranking Table
::: {.table-responsive}
```{python}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false

import os
import pandas as pd

summary_file = "downloads/volatility_summary.csv"
if os.path.exists(summary_file):
    df_vol = pd.read_csv(summary_file)
    
    # Rename columns slightly for clean table headers
    df_vol = df_vol.rename(columns={
        "Avg Daily Move (%)": "Avg. Daily Move",
        "Intraday Swing (%)": "Avg. Intraday Swing",
        "Annualized Volatility (%)": "Annualized Volatility",
        "Max Daily Gain (%)": "Max Daily Gain",
        "Max Daily Loss (%)": "Max Daily Loss"
    })
    
    # Format values as percentages with clean signs
    df_vol["Avg. Daily Move"] = df_vol["Avg. Daily Move"].map("{:.2f}%".format)
    df_vol["Avg. Intraday Swing"] = df_vol["Avg. Intraday Swing"].map("{:.2f}%".format)
    df_vol["Annualized Volatility"] = df_vol["Annualized Volatility"].map("{:.2f}%".format)
    df_vol["Max Daily Gain"] = df_vol["Max Daily Gain"].map("{:+.2f}%".format)
    df_vol["Max Daily Loss"] = df_vol["Max Daily Loss"].map("{:+.2f}%".format)
    
    # Render table manually with custom CSS classes applied
    print("<table class='table table-striped table-hover'>")
    print("<thead><tr>")
    print("<th>Ticker</th><th>Company Name</th><th>Avg. Daily Move</th><th>Avg. Intraday Swing</th><th>Annualized Volatility</th><th>Max Daily Gain</th><th>Max Daily Loss</th>")
    print("</tr></thead><tbody>")
    
    for idx, row in df_vol.iterrows():
        print("<tr>")
        print(f"<td><span class='badge-ticker'>{row['Ticker']}</span></td>")
        print(f"<td><strong>{row['Company']}</strong></td>")
        print(f"<td>{row['Avg. Daily Move']}</td>")
        print(f"<td>{row['Avg. Intraday Swing']}</td>")
        print(f"<td style='color:#38bdf8; font-weight:700;'>{row['Annualized Volatility']}</td>")
        print(f"<td class='trend-up'>{row['Max Daily Gain']}</td>")
        print(f"<td class='trend-down'>{row['Max Daily Loss']}</td>")
        print("</tr>")
        
    print("</tbody></table>")
else:
    print("<div class='alert alert-warning'>Volatility summary file not found. Run analyze_volatility.py first.</div>")
```
:::
:::

### Visualizing Volatility Profiles

To compare the volatility profiles of each company, we plot **Annualized Volatility** alongside **Average Intraday Price Swings**. This chart ranks the companies by overall price velocity and displays how much price action happens *within* a single trading session.

::: {.custom-card}
```{python}
#| label: volatility-plot
#| echo: false

import os
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

summary_file = "downloads/volatility_summary.csv"
if os.path.exists(summary_file):
    df = pd.read_csv(summary_file)
    # Sort ascending for horizontal bar chart rendering from top (highest) to bottom
    df_sorted = df.sort_values(by="Annualized Volatility (%)", ascending=True)
    
    # Create a side-by-side or dual horizontal bar chart
    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=1, cols=2,
        subplot_titles=("Annualized Volatility (Overall Speed)", "Avg. Intraday Swing (Day-Trading Spans)"),
        shared_yaxes=True,
        horizontal_spacing=0.08
    )
    
    # Color mapping gradient for the bars
    # Low volatility (CSCO ~25%) -> Cool Teal, High volatility (TSLA ~59%) -> Hot Crimson
    color_values = df_sorted["Annualized Volatility (%)"]
    
    # Add Annualized Volatility Bar
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            y=df_sorted["Company"],
            x=df_sorted["Annualized Volatility (%)"],
            orientation='h',
            name="Annualized Volatility",
            marker=dict(
                color=color_values,
                colorscale="bluered",
                line=dict(color='rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1)', width=1)
            ),
            hovertemplate="Company: %{y}<br>Annualized Volatility: %{x:.2f}%<extra></extra>",
            text=df_sorted["Annualized Volatility (%)"].map("{:.1f}%".format),
            textposition='inside',
            insidetextanchor='end'
        ),
        row=1, col=1
    )
    
    # Add Intraday Swing Bar
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            y=df_sorted["Company"],
            x=df_sorted["Intraday Swing (%)"],
            orientation='h',
            name="Intraday Swing",
            marker=dict(
                color=df_sorted["Intraday Swing (%)"],
                colorscale="portland",
                line=dict(color='rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1)', width=1)
            ),
            hovertemplate="Company: %{y}<br>Intraday Swing: %{x:.2f}%<extra></extra>",
            text=df_sorted["Intraday Swing (%)"].map("{:.1f}%".format),
            textposition='inside',
            insidetextanchor='end'
        ),
        row=1, col=2
    )
    
    fig.update_layout(
        template="plotly_dark",
        height=500,
        margin=dict(l=10, r=20, t=40, b=40),
        showlegend=False,
        plot_bgcolor="#0f172a",
        paper_bgcolor="#0b0f19",
        yaxis=dict(
            tickfont=dict(size=12, family="Outfit"),
        ),
        xaxis=dict(
            title="Volatility (%)",
            gridcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)",
            ticksuffix="%"
        ),
        xaxis2=dict(
            title="Swing (%)",
            gridcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)",
            ticksuffix="%"
        )
    )
    
    fig.show()
else:
    print("<div class='alert alert-warning'>Volatility summary file not found.</div>")
```
:::

::: {.custom-card .insight-card}
### Educated Volatility Insights & Trend Analysis

An analysis of the 10-year volatility data reveals several structural trends:

1. **The Beta/Volatility Hierarchy**:
   * **High Beta Growth (TSLA, AMD)**: At the top of the spectrum sit **Tesla** and **AMD** with annualized volatilities exceeding **56-59%**. These companies are characterized by rapid product cycles (semiconductor node shifts, electric vehicle scaling), intense competition, and high valuation multiples which make their prices highly sensitive to forward-looking growth estimates and macroeconomic liquidity.
   * **Growth Tech (NFLX, QCOM, META, AMZN)**: These companies sit in a middle band of **32-41%** volatility. While they are massive cash-flow engines, their stock prices are heavily impacted by discrete growth parameters (Netflix subscriber updates, Meta ad spend, Amazon margins).
   * **Enterprise & Diversified Value (SBUX, AAPL, MSFT, CSCO)**: Sitting below **30%** volatility, these businesses have massive scale, recurring revenue models (cloud subscriptions, product ecosystem lock-in, global retail footprints), and huge stock buyback programs that act as price shock-absorbers.

2. **The Intraday vs. Interday Swing Ratio**:
   * For **Tesla (TSLA)** and **AMD**, the average intraday range is **4.2%**, but their daily close-to-close move is **~2.5-2.6%**. This implies that these assets experience heavy "noise" and trading volume *during* the trading day (day-trading momentum), where prices swing widely but often settle closer to the previous day's close.
   * In contrast, mature assets like **Microsoft (MSFT)** have a very tight intraday swing (**1.9%**) and daily move (**1.18%**), indicating orderly, institutional trading flows with minimal speculative spikes.

3. **Asymmetric Tail Risk (Extreme Earnings Gaps)**:
   * Volatility is not always symmetrical. Looking at **Netflix (NFLX)** and **Meta (META)**, their maximum single-day drawdowns (**-35.12%** and **-26.39%** respectively) are significantly larger than their annualized volatility would predict. This points to the phenomenon of **"gap risk"**—where major growth revisions trigger massive capital re-allocations instantly, bypassing normal daily trading ranges. 
:::

## Detailed Stock Ingestion Charts

::: {.custom-card}
Select a tab below to view interactive historical price and volume charting (10-year limit) for each company, styled similarly to NASDAQ's Advanced Charting interface.

```{python}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false

import os
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

downloads_dir = "downloads"
ticker_names = {
    "AAPL": "Apple (AAPL)",
    "MSFT": "Microsoft (MSFT)",
    "AMZN": "Amazon (AMZN)",
    "TSLA": "Tesla (TSLA)",
    "META": "Meta (META)",
    "AMD": "AMD (AMD)",
    "NFLX": "Netflix (NFLX)",
    "SBUX": "Starbucks (SBUX)",
    "CSCO": "Cisco (CSCO)",
    "QCOM": "Qualcomm (QCOM)"
}

if os.path.exists(downloads_dir):
    csv_files = sorted([f for f in os.listdir(downloads_dir) if f.endswith("_historical.csv")])
    
    if csv_files:
        # Start Quarto Tabset
        print("::: {.panel-tabset}")
        
        for file in csv_files:
            ticker = file.replace("_historical.csv", "")
            company_label = ticker_names.get(ticker, f"{ticker} Stock")
            file_path = os.path.join(downloads_dir, file)
            
            # Read and parse CSV
            df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
            df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
            df = df.sort_values(by='date').reset_index(drop=True)
            
            # Identify volume direction colors (green for price gain, red for loss)
            colors = []
            prices = df['close'].values
            for i in range(len(df)):
                if i == 0:
                    colors.append('#10b981')
                else:
                    if prices[i] >= prices[i-1]:
                        colors.append('#10b981')
                    else:
                        colors.append('#ef4444')
            
            # Create subplots (Price top panel, Volume bottom panel)
            fig = make_subplots(
                rows=2, cols=1, 
                shared_xaxes=True, 
                vertical_spacing=0.05,
                row_heights=[0.75, 0.25]
            )
            
            # Add Area Chart for Price
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Scatter(
                    x=df['date'], 
                    y=df['close'],
                    name="Close Price",
                    line=dict(color="#38bdf8", width=2),
                    fill="tozeroy",
                    fillcolor="rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.1)",
                    hovertemplate="Date: %{x|%Y-%m-%d}<br>Price: $%{y:.2f}<extra></extra>"
                ),
                row=1, col=1
            )
            
            # Add Bar Chart for Volume
            fig.add_trace(
                go.Bar(
                    x=df['date'], 
                    y=df['volume'],
                    name="Volume",
                    marker=dict(color=colors, line=dict(width=0)),
                    hovertemplate="Volume: %{y:,}<extra></extra>"
                ),
                row=2, col=1
            )
            
            # Styling & Range Selectors
            fig.update_layout(
                template="plotly_dark",
                height=550,
                margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=10, b=20),
                showlegend=False,
                hovermode="x unified",
                xaxis2=dict(
                    rangeslider=dict(visible=False),
                    rangeselector=dict(
                        buttons=list([
                            dict(count=1, label="1Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                            dict(count=5, label="5Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                            dict(step="all", label="MAX (10Y)")
                        ]),
                        font=dict(color="#ffffff"),
                        bgcolor="rgba(30, 41, 59, 0.8)",
                        activecolor="#38bdf8"
                    ),
                    gridcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)"
                ),
                xaxis=dict(
                    gridcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)"
                ),
                yaxis=dict(
                    title="Stock Price ($)",
                    side="right",
                    gridcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05)",
                    tickprefix="$",
                    tickformat=".2f"
                ),
                yaxis2=dict(
                    title="Volume",
                    gridcolor="rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02)",
                    showticklabels=False
                ),
                plot_bgcolor="#0f172a",
                paper_bgcolor="#0b0f19"
            )
            
            # Print the tab header for Quarto
            print(f"### {company_label}\n")
            
            # Render and display the figure
            fig.show()
            print("\n")
            
        # End Quarto Tabset
        print(":::")
```
:::
